title: Contract Pricing Escalation & Billing Rules Engine — Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content: Summary: This playbook defines the Contract Pricing Escalation and Billing Rules Engine used by Redwood Inference to: (1) apply contractually-accurate pricing changes to invoices, (2) route pricing disputes and exceptions to the correct finance/legal/ops owners, and (3) ensure revenue recognition and billing automation behave predictably across hosted, dedicated and private deployment billing models. Scope and applicability: - Applies to all customer contract amendments, price adjustments, promotional credits, and capacity/commitment modifications for hosted API, Dedicated and Private products. - Excludes one-off partner integrations handled by Partner Ops (see related pages). - Effective for deals with signature date >= 2026-01-01; legacy deals are managed per Contract Amendment SOP. Goals and success metrics: - Automation coverage: 80% of routine price-change events should be handled end-to-end by the rules engine without manual intervention. - Billing accuracy: < 0.5% invoice adjustment rate caused by pricing logic errors. - Dispute SLA: 2 business days Triage, 10 business days Resolution for standard pricing disputes. Key concepts and definitions: - Pricing Rule: A discrete rule that maps contract terms (tier, region, feature flags, commitment band) to invoice line pricing and metadata. - Effective Window: Start/end timestamps when a pricing rule is valid for usage correlation. - Billing Token: Atomic meter unit used in invoicing (tokens for generation, embedding units, dedicated-GPU-hours). - Escalation Path: Pre-defined sequence of owners for exceptions (Billing Ops -> RevRec -> Legal -> Sales). Owners and contact points: - Billing Rules Engine Owner: Finance Systems (primary) — lead: Ethan Calder — billing-systems@redwood.ai - Legal Approval for Contract Changes: Legal Counsel — lead: Sofia Martinez — legal-contracts@redwood.ai - Revenue Recognition Owner: RevRec Team — lead: Daniel Cho — revrec@redwood.ai High-level architecture: - Ingestion: Contract ingestion service (contracts-api) converts signed contract PDFs/CLM entries into canonical JSON terms. - Rule Compiler: Translates contract terms into executable pricing rules applied by the Billing Rules Engine. - Execution: Billing Engine applies rules to usage events; results are stored in the invoice staging table and reconciled with ledger. - Observability: Per-customer rule application trace stored in the rules-audit index (retention 365 days). Example pricing-rule snippet (YAML): --- rule_id: dedicated-commit-band-42 priority: 200 match: product: dedicated region: eu-west-1 commitment_band: 1000-4999 actions: unit_price: 1.75 # USD per GPU-hour apply_credit: false revrec_mapping: committed_revenue effective_window: start: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z end: 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z --- Escalation matrix (rule exception types): 1) Mismatch between contract and compiled rule (Validation Error) - Auto-notify: Billing Systems + Legal (within 1 hour) - Triage owner: Billing Systems (2 business hours) - Escalate to Legal after 1 business day if unresolved 2) Disputed invoice due to price interpretation (Customer Dispute) - Auto-notify: CS Rep + Billing Ops + Sales AE - Triage owner: Billing Ops (2 business days) - Secondary: RevRec review if revenue impact > $10,000 3) Rule executable failure (Runtime) - Pager: On-call Billing SRE (pager after 10 minutes) - Fallback: Apply previous known-good rule and create corrective invoice if necessary Change control and approvals: - Minor pricing adjustments (<= 5% of contract list price and no revrec mapping changes): Finance Systems approval only (ticket in FIN-BILL queue). - Material changes (> 5% or any revrec mapping change): Legal + RevRec + Finance Systems sign-off. Sales Ops must attach ACORD form for delegated discounts. - All approved changes must be timestamped and stored in contracts-audit with the signer, ticket id, and rationale. Billing reconciliation & cutover checklist (when a rule changes mid-billing-cycle): 1) Freeze rule generation timestamp (T0) and snapshot current rule set. 2) Run pre-cutover dry-run against the billing-staging dataset. 3) Compare delta: - Net invoice delta <= $2,000 or <= 0.5% of run total -> allow automated cutover. - Otherwise -> require manual review and scheduled cutover window. 4) Post-cutover: auto-generate corrective invoices for retroactive deltas that meet schedule policy. Revenue recognition alignment: - Each pricing rule must declare revrec_mapping: committed_revenue | usage_revenue | other_specified. - Deferred revenue entries generated by the Billing Engine must include a source_rule_id and contract_signature_date. - RevRec team runs monthly reconciliation comparing rules-audit with general ledger; exceptions flagged for investigation within 5 business days. Dispute handling and customer credits: - Dispute window default: 60 days from invoice date unless contract specifies otherwise. - Temporary credits may be issued by Billing Ops up to $5,000 for low-risk disputes; amounts above require RevRec + Legal approval. - Credits must be delivered as invoice adjustments (negative invoice lines) or account-level credits with an expiry date. Operational runbook (common procedures): - Validate new contract ingestion: 1. Pull contract from CLM (contracts-api). 2. Run contract-compiler dry-run. 3. Check rule compilation log for warnings (SEV>0). 4. Approve and tag with approval ticket (FIN-BILL-XXXX). - Emergency rollback of a rule set: 1. Open FIN-BILL incident and notify RevRec + Legal. 2. Switch billing-engine to last-known-good ruleset (older snapshot). 3. Reprocess invoices affected during failure window and notify stakeholders. Audit, controls and evidence collection: - All rule changes must be logged in contracts-audit with: actor, timestamp, before/after JSON, approval ticket id. - Quarterly internal audit will sample 10% of rule changes, focusing on material discounts and revrec mapping changes. - Evidence retained for 7 years for regulated customers; default retention is 3 years. Appendix A — Threshold reference table: | Threshold name | Trigger | Unit | Owner | |---------------|---------:|------:|------------------| | Material Change | > 5% price delta | % | Legal + RevRec | | High Revenue Impact | > $10,000 | USD | RevRec | | Auto-credit ceiling | <= $5,000 | USD | Billing Ops | | Dispute window | 60 | days | Billing Ops | Appendix B — Example scenarios: - Scenario 1: Customer upgrades Dedicated commitment mid-month. Steps: Sales creates amendment, Contract ingestion runs, Billing Rules Engine compiles new rule with effective start aligned to amendment time. Dry-run performed; if delta small, automatic cutover; else scheduled cutover and customer notified. - Scenario 2: Promotional credit applied retroactively. Steps: Sales Ops creates promo ticket, Legal validates T&C, Billing Ops issues adjustment invoice with negative line and expiry metadata. RevRec maps to other_specified revenue. Related artifacts and links: - contracts-api onboarding guide (internal link) - FIN-BILL queue playbook (Jira board FIN-BILL) - RevRec monthly template (spreadsheet) Revision history: - 2025-11-15: Initial draft (Priya Nair) - 2026-01-28: Added automated cutover thresholds and YAML example (Ethan Calder) - 2026-02-20: Hardened dispute SLAs and retention notes (Sofia Martinez) Questions or change requests: Open a request in the FIN-BILL Confluence comments or file a Jira ticket (FIN-BILL) and tag the Billing Rules Engine owner.
